name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey (Gao et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2312.10997 (v1 submitted 18 Dec 2023; latest v5 27 Mar 2024). Subjects: cs.CL, cs.AI. Marked 'Ongoing Work'. Not formally peer-reviewed at a conference/journal; arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2312.10997.
authors_affiliation: Yunfan Gao (Shanghai Research Institute for Intelligent Autonomous Systems, Tongji University); Yun Xiong, Xinyu Gao, Kangxiang Jia, Jinliu Pan (Shanghai Key Laboratory of Data Science, School of Computer Science, Fudan University); Yuxi Bi, Meng Wang (College of Design and Innovation, Tongji University); Yi Dai, Jiawei Sun (Shanghai Research Institute for Intelligent Autonomous Systems, Tongji University); Haofen Wang (corresponding author; Shanghai Research Institute for Intelligent Autonomous Systems & College of Design and Innovation, Tongji University). 10 authors across Tongji University and Fudan University, China.
code_url: https://github.com/Tongji-KGLLM/RAG-Survey (maintained companion repository of RAG papers; the survey itself has no method code).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Tongji-KGLLM/RAG-Survey (Tongji-KGLLM RAG-Survey GitHub paper list maintained alongside the survey, organizing academic RAG papers under the LLM context; more current than the frozen PDF).
task_domain: Survey of RAG for LLMs. Primary task surveyed is knowledge-intensive QA (single-hop, multi-hop, long-form, multiple-choice, domain-specific), but the survey explicitly catalogs 26 downstream tasks including dialogue generation, information extraction, reasoning, fact verification, text summarization/classification, code search, machine translation, and recommendation. Not specifically about planning/agents/tool-use, though it touches agentic adaptive retrieval (WebGPT, Toolformer, Self-RAG) at the inference stage.
problem_setting: A comprehensive literature review (not a method). It synthesizes 100+ RAG studies and ~50 datasets into a paradigm taxonomy (Naive RAG -> Advanced RAG -> Modular RAG), analyzes the three core stages of every RAG pipeline (Retrieval, Generation, Augmentation), and reviews the evaluation landscape (targets, aspects, benchmarks, tools). The setting surveyed is predominantly offline, single-agent, non-interactive RAG over external knowledge bases for knowledge-intensive generation; supervision ranges from off-the-shelf (training-free ICL/inference) to fine-tuned retrievers/generators and end-to-end/collaborative training. The survey organizes RAG along the LLM lifecycle stages of pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference (the 'technology tree').
what_is_retrieved: Predominantly docs/text chunks from external knowledge bases. The survey's Table I enumerates retrieved units across surveyed methods: text (phrase, proposition, sentence, sentence-pair, chunk, document, item), knowledge-graph elements (entity, triplet, sub-graph), tabular data, code, and cross-lingual text. Also discusses LLM-internal/parametric 'retrieval' (RECITE, GenRead) and memory-pool retrieval (Self-Mem). Not focused on demos/cases/trajectories/skills/tools as in agentic-experience retrieval.
retrieval_grounding: Predominantly STATIC external corpus (Wikipedia, search engines, datasets, knowledge graphs like Freebase/CMeKG, pre-training corpora, BEIR, Common Crawl, arXiv/PubMed). The survey also covers HYBRID/generated-knowledge variants where the LLM generates context (Generate-Read, Recite-Read, PKG) and a 'Memory module' that builds an unbounded, iteratively self-enhanced memory pool (Self-Mem, Selfmem) - a growing store. Overall the dominant grounding surveyed is static external knowledge, with some hybrid/generative and memory-pool exceptions.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: The canonical RAG objective surveyed is a fixed top-k chunk ranking by semantic similarity (Naive RAG retrieves the Top K most-similar chunks). Advanced/Modular RAG add reranking and context selection/compression but still operate on a top-k-then-curate paradigm; the survey does not frame the objective as recovering a complete minimal set or as precision-driven variable-size recommendation. Multi-hop/iterative retrieval expands coverage across steps rather than enforcing per-call set completeness.
retrieval_unit: Surveyed as a spectrum of granularities (the survey devotes section III-A2 to 'Retrieval Granularity'). Table I lists: Phrase (CoG), Proposition (DenseX), Sentence, Sentence Pair, Item (TIGER/LM-Indexer recommendation items), Chunk (the dominant unit), Document/Doc, Multi (UniMS-RAG), plus KG units: Triplet, Entity, Entity Sequence, Sub-Graph (SURGE, G-Retriever). The default Naive-RAG unit is the text chunk (vectorized segment of a document).
index_source: Surveyed across the spectrum: predominantly static offline-built corpora (Wikipedia, datasets, KGs, pre-training corpora indexed in vector databases). The survey notes the 'augmentation stage' axis (Pre-training / Fine-tuning / Inference) for when the index/method is constructed. Also covers inference-time generated context (LLMs as a knowledge source: GenRead, RECITE, PKG) and self-enhanced growing memory pools (Self-Mem). So index source is mostly static external; some hybrid offline+online/generated variants.
index_structure_topology: The survey's section III-B (Indexing Optimization) and III-A (Retrieval Source / Data Structure) cover: flat vector indices (the Naive-RAG default vector database over chunks), metadata-attached indices (III-B2: metadata filtering, time-aware), structural/hierarchical indices (III-B3: hierarchical structural index, tree/summary structures e.g. RAPTOR, document trees), and knowledge-GRAPH indices (KGs/sub-graphs: SURGE, RoG, G-Retriever, HyKGE, KnowledGPT). So flat vector, metadata-keyed, hierarchical/tree, and graph topologies are all surveyed.
retriever_type: Surveyed broadly: dense embedding retrievers (the default; section III-D Embedding), sparse/keyword (BM25), mix/hybrid retrieval (III-D1, combining keyword+semantic+vector), fine-tuned/learned embedding models (III-D2), LLM-as-retriever / generative approaches (GenRead, RECITE generating context from model weights; LM-Indexer/TIGER generative item retrieval), and KG/graph retrievers. Adapter-based retrieval (III-E) is also covered. No single retriever is endorsed; the survey catalogs all types.
retriever_learning_signal: Surveyed across the full range: none/off-the-shelf (frozen dense or BM25 embeddings, training-free ICL), contrastive similarity training (fine-tuning embedding models, III-D2), LM-feedback signals (e.g. Rewrite-Retrieve-Read uses an LM-feedback mechanism to update the rewriting model; AAR uses LLM preferences; UPRISE, LLM-R train retrievers from LM signal), downstream-task-effectiveness, and end-to-end / collaborative fine-tuning of retriever+generator (RA-DIT, Atlas, RePLUG, BGM bridge model). Reinforcement learning is surveyed for adaptive retrieval/agents (WebGPT trains GPT-3 with RL to use a search engine). The survey frames retriever training along an Adapter/embedding-fine-tuning/RL spectrum.
query_construction: Surveyed in section III-C (Query Optimization): raw query (Naive RAG), query expansion (III-C1: multi-query, sub-queries, Chain-of-Verification), query transformation (III-C2: query rewriting via RRR/Rewrite-Retrieve-Read, HyDE hypothetical document embeddings, step-back prompting), and query routing (III-C3: routing to data sources/sub-pipelines). Iterative/recursive augmentation reconstructs queries from generated CoT/intermediate text (IRCoT, ITER-RETGEN, ToC clarification tree). So raw, expanded, rewritten/transformed, decomposed, and thought-conditioned query construction are all covered.
query_granularity: Surveyed at multiple levels. Default is task-level (one query at t=0 -> top-k). The augmentation chapter (V) covers trajectory/step-level query construction: iterative retrieval re-queries based on accumulated generation; recursive retrieval refines queries and decomposes into sub-problems (IRCoT uses CoT to guide each retrieval step); adaptive retrieval issues retrieval mid-generation (FLARE per upcoming-sentence, Self-RAG per segment). So task-level, trajectory-level, and step/state-level query granularities are all surveyed.
when_to_retrieve: Surveyed as four modes (the organizing axis of section V and Table I's 'Retrieval process' column): Once (single retrieval before generation, the Naive-RAG default), Iterative (alternating retrieval and generation), Recursive (progressive query refinement / problem decomposition; also multi-hop on graphs), and Adaptive (the system autonomously decides whether/when to retrieve, e.g. FLARE, Self-RAG, SKR). Some entries are 'Multi-time'.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Surveyed concrete WHEN-to-retrieve signals in section V-C (Adaptive Retrieval): (a) fixed schedule (Once/Iterative-RETGEN fixed rounds); (b) token-level generation confidence/probability (FLARE monitors the probability of generated terms and triggers retrieval when below a threshold); (c) reflection/special tokens (Self-RAG emits 'retrieve' and 'critic' reflection tokens; WebGPT emits special action tokens for search/browse/cite); (d) learned classifier of self-knowledge (SKR judges whether the model already knows). The survey frames adaptive retrieval as the LLM exercising active judgment like an agent (AutoGPT, Toolformer, Graph-Toolformer).
reranking: Yes - reranking is a first-class topic. Section IV-A1 (Reranking, under Context Curation in Generation) and the Advanced-RAG post-retrieval process cover relocating the most-relevant content to prompt edges, cross-encoder/rule-based and model-based rerankers, and RAG-Fusion's intelligent re-ranking after multi-query parallel search. Reranking is presented as a core post-retrieval / Advanced-RAG strategy implemented in LlamaIndex/LangChain/Haystack.
retrieved_context_refinement: Surveyed extensively in section IV-A (Context Curation): reranking (IV-A1) and context selection/compression (IV-A2). Covered operations include reranking, context compression (RECOMP, PRCA, Token-Elimination/Long-context token reduction), selecting/emphasizing essential information to avoid information overload, noise filtering (FILCO, FILTER-rerank, CoN/Chain-of-Note), and the Predict module (GenRead generating context to reduce redundancy/noise). So none/rerank/decompose/distill/filter/compress are all surveyed.
how_retrieved_used: Predominantly prompt augmentation: retrieved chunks are synthesized with the query into a prompt for the LLM (the Naive/Advanced-RAG default). The survey also covers training-signal uses - retrieval integrated at the pre-training stage (Atlas, RETRO++, RAVEN), fine-tuning stage (RA-DIT, generator fine-tuning), and via adapters/intermediate modules (III-E Adapter, BGM bridge model) and latent integration. The 'how' is organized along the augmentation stage axis (pre-training / fine-tuning / inference).
planning_integration: As a RAG (not planning/agent) survey, planning integration is mostly out of scope; the closest analog is the augmentation-process taxonomy (section V): plan-then-retrieve and retrieve-then-plan analogs appear as recursive retrieval with problem decomposition into sub-problems (IRCoT chain-of-thought-guided retrieval, ToC clarification tree, DSP Demonstrate-Search-Predict) and iterative retrieve-read loops (ITER-RETGEN). Adaptive retrieval embeds the retrieve decision inside generation. There is no MCTS/tree-search planner or explicit hierarchical subtask planner surveyed.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Surveyed at several granularities: per-answer (Once retrieval), per-CoT-step (recursive retrieval, IRCoT interleaves a reasoning step with a retrieval step; ITER-RETGEN alternates retrieval-augmented-generation and generation-augmented-retrieval each round), and per-sentence/per-token (adaptive retrieval: FLARE triggers retrieval per upcoming sentence based on token confidence; Self-RAG operates per segment with fragment-level beam search). Per-tool-call is touched via WebGPT/agentic special tokens.
retrieved_item_representation: Predominantly raw retrieved text (chunks/documents/passages) injected as prompt context. The survey also covers distilled/compressed representations (context compression, summaries in hierarchical/recursive retrieval, RAPTOR summary nodes), generated/predicted context (GenRead, PKG), structured KG triples/sub-graphs (SURGE, RoG, G-Retriever), and notes (Chain-of-Note). The dominant surface form is raw text; refinement produces compressed/summarized/structured variants.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mostly raw retrieved passages/chunks (no distilled strategy or procedural skill - this is classic knowledge RAG, not experience/skill retrieval). Higher-abstraction units surveyed include summaries (RAPTOR recursive summarization, hierarchical structural index), propositions (DenseX), and KG sub-graphs/triples (structured relational abstraction). The survey does not retrieve strategies/workflows/skills in the agentic-experience sense.
noise_robustness_mechanism: A central evaluation aspect and discussion topic. Methods surveyed for guarding against irrelevant/incorrect context: relevance evaluation / self-reflection (Self-RAG critic tokens, CRAG corrective retrieval), reason-in-documents / note-taking (CoN Chain-of-Note), distractor filtering and context compression (FILCO, FILTER-rerank, RECOMP, NoiseRAG study), and retriever-aware / robustness-targeted training (RAG-Robust, NoMIRACL for negative/no-relevant-doc rejection). Section VII-B (RAG Robustness) discusses how noise and even counterfactual/adversarial documents affect RAG, and evaluation aspect 'Noise Robustness', 'Negative Rejection', and 'Counterfactual Robustness' formalize it.
memory_type: Mostly none (classic RAG over static external knowledge). The survey does cover a 'Memory module' in Modular RAG (II-C1): leveraging the LLM's memory to guide retrieval, creating an unbounded memory pool aligned to data distribution through iterative self-enhancement (Self-Mem). So an episodic/self-enhancing memory-pool type is surveyed as one module, but it is not the dominant paradigm.
write_back: Mostly false for canonical RAG (the external index is static). Exception surveyed: the Memory module (Self-Mem) writes back self-generated/selected memories into an unbounded, iteratively self-enhanced memory pool. As a survey it documents both static (no write-back) and self-enhancing (write-back) variants; write-back is the minority case.
online_growth: Predominantly false (the vector index is frozen after offline construction; retrieval is read-only at inference). The surveyed Memory module / Self-Mem is the exception where the memory pool grows via iterative self-enhancement at inference. The dominant surveyed paradigm has no online growth.
write_back_trigger: Mostly never (static external corpus, read-only retrieval). For the minority Memory-module / Self-Mem case surveyed, writes are reflective/self-enhancement-triggered (the model iteratively generates candidate memories and selects/retains the better ones to align the pool with the data distribution). No on-success/on-failure experience-logging trigger is a focus, since this is knowledge RAG not experience RAG.
failure_experience_usage: Not a focus (knowledge RAG does not store success/failure experiences). The closest related ideas surveyed are negative/distractor handling at training time (RAG-Robust, NoMIRACL negative-rejection, FILCO filtering) and counterfactual-robustness evaluation - i.e. handling incorrect retrieved documents, not storing the agent's own failed trajectories. No success-vs-failure contrastive experience memory is surveyed as a paradigm.
memory_evolution_update: Mostly N/A (static external index; no stored experiential entries to mutate). For the Self-Mem memory-pool exception the dynamic is iterative refine/self-enhancement (regenerate-and-select to improve the pool). Indexing optimization (re-chunking, metadata, hierarchical re-structuring, RAPTOR summarization) is an offline index-construction operation rather than online entry mutation.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Surveyed as a spectrum but the dominant paradigm is fixed similarity top-k, not a learned policy. Learned/optimized variants covered: RL-trained retrieval/search action selection (WebGPT trains GPT-3 with reinforcement learning to use a search engine), learned query routing (III-C3), learned adaptive-retrieval triggers (Self-RAG reflection tokens, SKR self-knowledge classifier), and end-to-end trained retriever-generator (RePLUG, RA-DIT, Atlas, BGM). No M-MDP / soft-Q case-selection policy (out of scope for a knowledge-RAG survey).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Not a focus / largely N/A. The survey covers single-system RAG pipelines; it does not center collective or cross-agent shared memory. It does note that the Modular-RAG flexible architecture can integrate other technologies and that adaptive retrieval mirrors agent tool-use (AutoGPT, Toolformer), but no explicit cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing is surveyed.
benchmarks: Catalogs ~50 datasets across 26 tasks (Table II). QA: Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, SQuAD, WebQuestions, PopQA, MS MARCO (single-hop); HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue (multi-hop); ELI5, NarrativeQA, ASQA, QMSum (long-form); Qasper, COVID-QA, CMB, MMCU_Medical (domain); QuALITY, ARC, CommonsenseQA (multiple-choice); GraphQA. Dialogue: Wizard of Wikipedia, KBP, DuLeMon, CamRest, Amazon (recommendation). IE: WikiEvent, RAMS, T-REx, ZsRE. Reasoning: HellaSwag, CoT, CSQA, StrategyQA. Others: MMLU, WikiText-103, FEVER, PubHealth, Biography, WikiASP, XSum, VioLens, TREC, SST-2, CodeSearchNet, NoMIRACL, GSM8K, JRC-Acquis. RAG-specific evaluation benchmarks: RGB, RECALL, CRUD; tools: RAGAS, ARES, TruLens, RALLE.
benchmark_family: QA (single-hop NQ/TriviaQA/SQuAD/WebQ/PopQA/MS MARCO), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA/2WikiMultiHopQA/MuSiQue), long-form QA (ELI5/NarrativeQA/ASQA/QMSum), domain QA (Qasper/COVID-QA/CMB), multiple-choice QA (QuALITY/ARC/CommonsenseQA), dialogue, information extraction, reasoning (StrategyQA/CSQA/HellaSwag/GSM8K), fact-checking (FEVER/PubHealth), summarization, classification/sentiment, code search (CodeSearchNet), machine translation, recommendation, and RAG-robustness (NoMIRACL). Plus dedicated RAG evaluation families: RGB/RECALL/CRUD benchmarks and RAGAS/ARES/TruLens tools. Not the agent/web/embodied/tool benchmark families (Mind2Web/WebArena/ALFWorld/ToolBench) of the agentic-RAG literature.
baselines: N/A (a survey, not a method - it runs no head-to-head experiments and reports no baseline comparison table of its own). It compares RAG conceptually against Fine-tuning (FT) and Prompt Engineering along the axes of 'External Knowledge Required' vs 'Model Adaptation Required' (Figure 4), and against Long-Context LLMs (section VII-A), citing that RAG consistently outperforms unsupervised fine-tuning on knowledge-intensive tasks.
key_metrics: Surveys the metrics rather than reporting its own. Task metrics: EM, F1, Accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE/ROUGE-L (Table III). Retrieval-quality metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, NDCG, Recall, Precision. RAG-specific aspect metrics: R-Rate (Reappearance Rate, for counterfactual robustness), Cosine Similarity, BertScore, RAGQuestEval, plus the RAGAS/ARES triad scores (Context Relevance, Faithfulness, Answer Relevance). Table III maps each metric to the seven evaluation aspects.
headline_result: N/A (no single experimental headline number - it is a review). Its headline conceptual contribution is the three-paradigm taxonomy Naive RAG -> Advanced RAG -> Modular RAG plus the tripartite 'Retrieval / Generation / Augmentation' decomposition, and an evaluation framework of 3 quality scores (Context Relevance, Faithfulness, Answer Relevance) and 4 abilities (Noise Robustness, Negative Rejection, Information Integration, Counterfactual Robustness), synthesized from 100+ RAG studies, 26 tasks, and ~50 datasets.
ablations: N/A (no experiments, hence no ablations). The analytical equivalent is the comparative framing: (1) the paradigm comparison (Naive vs Advanced vs Modular RAG, Figure 3) showing which components/strategies address which Naive-RAG failure modes; (2) the RAG-vs-Fine-tuning-vs-Prompt-Engineering quadrant (Figure 4); (3) the augmentation-process comparison (Once vs Iterative vs Recursive vs Adaptive, Figure 5); (4) the RAG-vs-Long-Context discussion (VII-A).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes - the survey explicitly separates Retrieval Quality (intrinsic IR metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, NDCG, Context Relevance) from Generation Quality (Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE) as the two 'Evaluation Targets' (section VI-B), and maps metrics/abilities to each (Table III, Table IV). It advocates measuring retrieval and generation separately, which is precisely the decoupling principle.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, and the survey argues process quality matters. Outcome: task accuracy/EM/F1/BLEU/ROUGE. Process: Context Relevance and retrieval IR metrics (Hit Rate/MRR/NDCG) score the retrieval step; Faithfulness scores whether generation is grounded in retrieved context (a process-faithfulness measure); the four 'required abilities' (Noise Robustness, Negative Rejection, Information Integration, Counterfactual Robustness) probe intermediate behavior beyond final-answer correctness.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively rather than measured. The survey notes RAG is cost-effective vs native LLMs and vs retraining (FT), but incurs higher inference latency and retrieval overhead; context compression/selection (IV-A2) and token elimination are surveyed to cut prompt length/cost; the RAG-vs-Long-Context discussion (VII-A) weighs retrieval cost against feeding long context; 'Scaling laws of RAG' (VII-D) and 'Production-Ready RAG' (VII-E) raise efficiency/engineering tradeoffs. No quantitative latency/token/API-cost numbers are reported by the survey itself.
context_budget_and_selection_count: The canonical RAG budget lever surveyed is Top-K chunk selection by similarity, then post-retrieval reranking-then-truncation and context compression (IV-A2) to fit the LLM context window and avoid information overload / 'lost in the middle'. The survey discusses chunking strategy (III-B1, chunk size/overlap, sliding window) as the granularity-vs-budget tradeoff. k is typically fixed but adaptive/iterative variants change the effective number of retrieved items across steps. No single numeric budget is prescribed.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: (1) the three-paradigm evolution Naive RAG / Advanced RAG / Modular RAG; (2) the tripartite RAG foundation Retrieval / Generation / Augmentation; (3) the LLM-lifecycle 'technology tree' axis: pre-training / fine-tuning / inference; (4) Table I axes per method: Retrieval Source, Retrieval Data Type, Retrieval Granularity, Augmentation Stage, Retrieval Process (Once/Iterative/Recursive/Adaptive); (5) evaluation axes: 2 targets, 3 quality scores, 4 abilities. Coverage: 100+ RAG studies, 26 downstream tasks, ~50 datasets; reference count ~169 (numbered citations to bib169); time window roughly 2020-2023 with v5 revised March 2024.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark paper - it does not construct a new dataset). It instead catalogs existing benchmarks/tools (RGB, RECALL, CRUD benchmarks; RAGAS, ARES, TruLens, RALLE tools) and ~50 task datasets, summarizing each framework's evaluation targets, aspects, and metrics in Table IV.
builds_on: Foundational pre-LLM RAG and retrieval-augmented LM work: the original RAG (Lewis et al. 2020), REALM, RETRO/RETRO++, Atlas, kNN-LM, DPR; in-context learning with ChatGPT/GPT-3.5. Builds conceptually on the Retrieve-Read framework and on prior component lines: query optimization (HyDE, query rewriting), reranking, context compression (RECOMP), iterative/recursive retrieval (IRCoT, ITER-RETGEN, DSP), and adaptive retrieval (FLARE, Self-RAG, WebGPT). Evaluation framework builds on RGB, RECALL, CRUD, RAGAS, ARES, TruLens.
contrasts_with: Positions RAG against (1) Fine-tuning (FT) and (2) Prompt Engineering as alternative LLM-optimization strategies (Figure 4 quadrant: External Knowledge vs Model Adaptation), arguing RAG consistently outperforms unsupervised fine-tuning for knowledge injection; (3) Long-Context LLMs (VII-A), arguing RAG remains valuable for efficiency/updatability despite growing context windows; and (4) within RAG, contrasts Naive vs Advanced vs Modular paradigms and Once vs Iterative/Recursive/Adaptive augmentation. Also contrasts with concurrent RAG surveys (e.g. by being the most-cited foundational RAG paradigm survey).
lineage: Surveys lineage. This is the canonical, most-cited foundational RAG survey (Group: Surveys), defining the Naive->Advanced->Modular RAG vocabulary widely adopted thereafter. It anchors the RAG-for-LLMs literature and is a precursor to later, more specialized surveys (agentic RAG, graph RAG, multimodal RAG, RAG evaluation). It sits upstream of the agentic/experience-retrieval works in this collection by establishing the static-corpus knowledge-RAG baseline that adaptive/iterative methods (FLARE, Self-RAG, IRCoT, Adaptive-RAG) extend.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning work; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle. It is a knowledge-RAG survey.)
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The survey does not frame RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it treats RAG as retrieval-augmented generation over external knowledge.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (the survey is not about tool/skill retrieval; it focuses on document/knowledge retrieval. It touches tool-use only via agentic adaptive-retrieval examples like Toolformer/WebGPT, without analyzing tool-description engineering for indexing.)
index_content_separation: N/A as a method, but the survey covers the related pattern under hierarchical/structural indexing (III-B3) and recursive retrieval (V-B): a lightweight summary/structural index can be searched first, then the heavier underlying document content retrieved on demand (e.g. summarize sections, then retrieve within the document; RAPTOR's tree of summaries). Not framed as progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool API / RapidAPI / MCP / function-calling tool index; static document/KG vector indices. The 'Search module' in Modular RAG can issue queries to search engines/databases/KGs via LLM-generated code/query languages, but this is not a synchronized tool registry with CRUD auto-sync.)
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; the survey covers document/KG retrieval, not multi-tool dependency graphs).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation/revision cycle - knowledge RAG injects retrieved text as context rather than adapting a retrieved case. The closest analog is post-retrieval context curation/compression and corrective retrieval, but that is refinement of context, not CBR-style case adaptation.)
